item.text: {"text":"[MARS (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.00702) offers the closest architectural idea: preserve multiple attribute-aware representations and match user interests to candidate attributes, rather than compressing all text into one vector. Its pretrained-language-model setting does not establish effectiveness from scratch. [JEPA4Rec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.10512) explores masked prediction of item-text representations and reduced reliance on large-scale pretraining, but does not directly validate the constrained BERT4Rec setup. [FineRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12975) learns attribute-specific representations with interaction-driven fusion; its review-derived opinions and LLM extraction are unavailable here.\n\nPractical adaptation hypothesis: jointly train a small token-embedding encoder over available titles/descriptions, using mean pooling as a cheap baseline or a shallow CNN/attention pooling layer for phrase-sensitive features. Fuse its output with item-ID embeddings through a learned residual gate inside one BERT4Rec network; optionally use a few learned pooling queries to retain distinct textual aspects. These are proposed experiments, not verified gains from the cited papers. Preserve masked-item training and appended-mask inference; hide both ID and text at masked positions to prevent target leakage. Encode only unique items needed per batch and cache catalog representations after training. Compare ID-only, pooled-text, and multi-aspect variants using the fixed macro validation HR@10. Treat compatibility, ownership, opinions, and simulator traits as unobserved; textual similarity alone supplies no labels for them."}
